character.motivation: Keeps family seeds and suspects his father benefited from the flood deal. Wants to name the debt in public himself.
character.voice: Dry wit, careful qualifiers, plant metaphors used sparingly.
character.backstory: Elias learned seed saving from his father, who accepted a dry plot after the council sold the flooded land. The seed merchant has kept the old jars even as he has grown uneasy about what made the family business possible.
character.quest_hook: Help Elias trace which families supplied the seeds, then ask them whether they want seed shares, credit, or both.

dialogue.introduction: I keep the crooked seeds. Sometimes those are the only ones that remember how to grow here.
dialogue.friendship: I can't prove my crooked seeds grow better. I can tell you which jar I reach for when it's my field.
dialogue.supper: I brought a jar for the table. People kept asking what was in it. Next year I'd like them to know.
dialogue.hearing: My father accepted one of those dry plots. I'd rather put his name in the record myself.
dialogue.date: I'll save you a seat by the seed trays. Tell me which one you'd plant if you had to leave before harvest.
dialogue.partner: Yes. I've already put two chairs by the seed trays. You can pick which one is yours.
dialogue.favorite_gift: A good turnip. Would you let me see the seed it came from?
dialogue.disliked_gift: I have nowhere dry to keep the grass. The nursery could use it.

routine.home_context: Stores his family's seed jars in a dry house close to the market road.
